chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Al-Nawfali, from Al-Sakuni, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Beware of smelling the bread as the wild beasts smell it, for the bread is blessed. Allah, Mighty and Majestic, sent down the sky for it with torrential rain, and for it Allah caused the pasture to grow, and by it you pray, and by it you fast, and by it you perform Hajj to the House of your Lord.'
ai.seo_question: What is the significance of bread in Shia Islamic tradition according to the hadith from Al-Kafi?
ai.summary: In al-Kafi, this hadith from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) links the physical act of smelling bread to spiritual greed, contrasting the 'beastly' manner of consumption with mindful gratitude. It underscores bread's unique status as a medium for worship, noting that prayer, fasting, and Hajj are physically sustained by it, thereby elevating daily sustenance to an act of devotion. This reflects the Shia emphasis on integrating mundane actions with spiritual awareness through the lens of divine barakah.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Al Nowfaly, from Al Sakuny, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:

‘Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> said: ‘Beware of smelling the bread just as you smell the wild animals smell it, for the bread is Blessed. Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Mighty and Majestic has Commanded the sky for it for torrential downpour, and for Allah<sup>azwj</sup> has Grown the meadows, and by it you are Praying, and by it you are Fasting, and by it you are performing the Hajj of the House of your Lord<sup>azwj</sup>’.
en.sarwar: 6. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from al-Nawfaliy from al-Sakuniy who has said the following: “Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said that the Messenger of Allah, O Allah, grant compensation to Muhammad and his family worthy of their services to Your cause, has said, ‘

You must never smell bread like the beasts do. Bread is blessed and Allah, most Majestic, most Glorious, has sent the sky with rain and because of it He has grown the pastures. By means of bread you perform Salat (prayer), observe fast and perform al-Hajj of the House of your Lord.’”
